title: Bangla enters the constitutional debate
detail: Dhirendranath Datta demanded that Bangla be used in Pakistan's Constituent Assembly. The proposal turned language into a constitutional question almost immediately after partition.

title: Strike and student mobilization spread across East Bengal
detail: A general strike was observed to protest the exclusion of Bangla from official use, coins, stamps, and recruitment tests. Student organizers, cultural activists, and progressive groups widened the movement.

title: Jinnah reaffirms Urdu as the sole state language
detail: During his Dhaka visit, Muhammad Ali Jinnah declared that Urdu alone would be the state language of Pakistan. The statement intensified public anger rather than ending the dispute.

title: The movement reorganizes and deepens
detail: Committees, student groups, writers, and cultural circles kept the language demand alive. By 1951, the issue had become linked to broader grievances over representation and inequality in East Bengal.

title: Khwaja Nazimuddin repeats the Urdu-only line
detail: Prime Minister Khwaja Nazimuddin publicly restated that Urdu would remain the only state language of Pakistan. The announcement pushed the movement into a decisive new phase.

title: All-Party State Language Action Committee is formed
detail: Leaders and activists assembled at Dhaka Bar Library and formed a broad action committee, with Kazi Golam Mahbub as convener, to coordinate the next phase of protest.

title: Section 144 is imposed in Dhaka
detail: The government banned assemblies in an attempt to stop demonstrations. Movement leaders debated whether the ban should be defied.

title: Students defy the ban and police open fire
detail: Students gathered on the Dhaka University and Medical College campus, chose to violate Section 144, and marched out in groups. Police baton-charged, used tear gas, and finally opened fire, killing and fatally wounding demonstrators including Barkat, Rafiq, Jabbar, and Salam.

title: Mass grief turns into a public symbol
detail: Protests spread further, Shafiur Rahman was killed on 22 February, and students rapidly built the first Shaheed Minar on 23 February at the site of the shootings.

title: Bangla is recognized as a state language
detail: The Constitution of Pakistan finally recognized Bangla as one of the state languages. The movement's political and emotional victory became a permanent part of Bengali national consciousness.
